title: Custom IAM policies must add ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes (mandatory in a future release)

detection.reason: the controller's IAM policy is AWS-side; IRSA shows only the role ARN and EKS Pod Identity nothing at all

quote: If you use a custom IAM policy, you will need to add `DescribeInstanceTypes` to your policy.
remediation: Add ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes to a custom EBS CSI policy now. From v1.59 the driver calls it to handle instances with several EBS cards and falls back to a built-in table when denied; a later release removes the fallback. The AWS-managed policies include it. The new least-privilege managed policies (issue #2918) are NOT a drop-in swap: they require the ebs.csi.aws.com/cluster-name tag (written only from v1.58 and only with --k8s-tag-cluster-id) or, for PolicyV2, ebs.csi.aws.com/cluster=true on static volumes — moving to them breaks attach/detach/delete/snapshot of volumes created before v1.58, without --k8s-tag-cluster-id, or statically provisioned without the tag.
verifyCommand: aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn ROLE_ARN --action-names ec2:DescribeInstanceTypes --query 'EvaluationResults[].[EvalActionName,EvalDecision]' --output text  # ROLE_ARN = the controller's role: the eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn annotation on ebs-csi-controller-sa (IRSA) or aws eks list-pod-identity-associations --cluster-name CLUSTER_NAME --namespace NAMESPACE --service-account ebs-csi-controller-sa; anything but 'allowed' means the driver falls back to its built-in table today and breaks when the fallback is removed
coversNotes: URGENT (1.59.0): The EBS CSI Driver now calls DescribeInstanceTypes at runtime to determine if an instance
